description:
## Goal and approved deferral

Upgrade arithmetic failure from the deliberately loud fatal endpoint accepted for fz-5xp.30 to a proper language exception. Keep the foreign arithmetic ABI, real runtime functions, result/status lanes and native substitutions unchanged.

The user's immediate requirement is satisfied in .30 by total arithmetic exports plus one obvious replacement point:

```fz
defp arithmetic_error(), do: panic(:badarith)
```

Every arithmetic wrapper calls that helper only after a returned failure status. For .30 a diagnostic followed by fatal termination is acceptable. Catchability, graceful teardown, full source/stack reporting and interpreter/REPL-host survival are NOT prerequisites for .30. This ticket remains open for the later stronger behavior; do not claim that loud panic completes proper exception handling.

## Historical failure and retained purpose

The original division-zero witness produced a Rust panic across an extern boundary in the interpreter and silent SIGILL in native execution. .30 removes arithmetic failure from the foreign side: checked exports return initialized {result, failed}; wrappers choose panic, and the user accepts that loud stop for now. This ticket no longer asks another agent to redo those arithmetic exports or build a rival checked-arithmetic/error-side-channel subsystem.

## Strategy when this follow-on is selected

1. Inspect the then-current language exception/error machinery, existing panic/fault completion and .30's single arithmetic_error definition. Present facts and the exception plan to the user before construction, as required for each new ticket. If general exception support is still absent, explicitly plan its minimum shared prerequisite using existing tickets; do not quietly expand this into a full exception framework.
2. Choose the language exception reason/type and source-context delivery through the ordinary shared exception mechanism. Replace the helper's panic implementation at that one point. The C arithmetic functions continue to return data and must not raise, unwind, abort or set hidden exception state.
3. Test handling and unhandled delivery through interpreter/REPL, JIT and AOT. Preserve cleanup and host survival to the extent promised by the agreed exception mechanism, with explicit tests rather than assuming the old panic path provided them.
4. Remove the temporary arithmetic panic body and any error plumbing actually displaced by the shared exception path. Keep general panic semantics separate if the language still intentionally supports fatal panic.

## Acceptance

- A handled arithmetic error is catchable and named consistently, and the host can continue serving another request. An unhandled one has a clear diagnostic and the agreed source context and process lifecycle.
- Cover div/rem/% zero, checked overflow, MIN/-1 division vs remainder, and floating failure using .30's established semantic contract; do not change numeric policy as part of exception delivery.
- Ordinary success behavior, allocation counts, physical C signatures, result/status transport and optimized machine arithmetic remain unchanged. No new check of process exception state is added after ordinary foreign calls.
- One central arithmetic_error replacement serves every wrapper. No operation-specific raise implementation or duplicate renderer/exception authority.
- Update relevant language-error, Kernel and extern docs. TDD, focused and full relevant gates, fresh cold Sol-high ticket-scoped review, one commit/close and prompt stack push.

## Order

fz-5xp.30 -> fz-5xp.32 -> this ticket. This is a later exception upgrade after the physical extern boundary is closed; it must not block .30 or .32. fz-5xp.20 wrapper inlining is independent and must preserve either panic or exception control flow.

Larger aggregate FFI features and a language-wide arithmetic rewrite are out of scope. Astra requires explicit permission.
title: Replace the shared arithmetic panic endpoint with proper Fz exceptions
